plan.notes: Transcribed 2026-09-30 from the official UMass Dartmouth Department of Computer & Information Science curriculum page (https://www.umassd.edu/engineering/cis/undergraduate/curriculum-and-courses/bachelor-of-science-in-computer-science/, 'Total Credits: 120', fetched live 2026-09-30). Degree name per the UMass Dartmouth catalog: 'BS degree in Computer Science'; the catalog's current published edition is the 2025-2026 Undergraduate Catalog (published July 2025), so catalog_year=2025-2026. Prerequisites cross-checked against the official CIS checkoff sheet 'Requirements for Bachelor of Science in Computer Science, Catalog Year 2021-22 to present' (t.umassd.edu, updated 11/10/2025) and the catalog's course listings. Semester totals as printed on the curriculum page: 14+14+15+14+16+16+16+15 = 120, which matches the catalog's own 'Total credits: 120' exactly; no discrepancy. Title choices: CIS 190 uses the catalog/checkoff title 'Introduction to Procedural Programming' (the curriculum overview page renders it as 'Systems Programming'); CIS 180/181 use the catalog titles 'Object-Oriented Programming I/II'; ENL 266 uses the catalog title 'Technical Communication'; CIS 481 uses the checkoff title 'Parallel and Distributed Software Systems' (overview page renders 'Parallel & Distributed Computing'). The current sequence places CIS 246 Foundations of Secure Computing (3 cr) in sophomore spring; no official prerequisite is published for CIS 246 on the curriculum page or the checkoff sheet, so its prereq list is empty rather than invented. CIS 272's catalog entry is a corequisite (Co: CIS 190, MTH 181) taken in the same term, encoded as empty prereq with this note. MTH 181 requires placement into MTH 153 (MTH 150/MTH 100 path delays calculus and may extend the program beyond four years per the catalog); MTH 154's catalog prereq reads 'MTH 153 or 151' and the math-elective slot reads 'MTH 154 or 152' - the alternate MTH 151/152 routes are documented here, not encoded, because those courses are not part of this plan. Lab Science I must be PHY 113, or CHM 151+161, or BIO 121+131; Lab Science II must be the continuation (PHY 114, CHM 152+162, or BIO 122+132); the Science Elective may be any course in BIO, CHM, MAR, MLS, or PHY and ideally either the lab-science or science-elective choice also satisfies University Studies Cluster 2A. University Studies slots must be chosen from Clusters 3 and 4 (catalog: Clusters 3 and 4 = 15 credits; Clusters 1, 2B, 5 are satisfied by required major courses). Technical electives: four courses from the approved CIS technical elective list, each with a grade of C or better; technical electives count in the major GPA. Catalog rules carried verbatim: any CIS core course or technical elective that is a prerequisite to another CIS course must be passed with a grade of C or better to satisfy the prerequisite; minimum 2.000 cumulative GPA and 2.000 major GPA to graduate; all majors complete the CIS Department Exit Survey in the final semester. Nothing invented; every course code, title, credit value, term placement, and prereq comes from the sources above.
